$description: Promoted from tokens/primitive/effect.json. These were always INTENT names — `modal`, `tooltip`, `backdrop`, `hover-overlay` describe a job in the UI, not raw material — so tier 1 was the wrong home and every component reading them was breaking the read-tier-2 rule through no fault of its own. Names are unchanged; only the tier moved.

overlay-hover.$description: Neutral wash for hover on a surface that has no colour of its own. `overlay` is a fourth property alongside background/content/border — a deliberate exception. These are translucent washes applied OVER a background rather than backgrounds themselves, and calling one `background-hover` would collide with the opaque gray-4 that already owns that name.

overlay-hover-strong.$description: As above, where the surface needs more separation. Aliases the black-alpha ramp — the value was already exactly this step.

overlay-hover-heavy.$description: The heaviest wash — a control that sits ON a tinted surface and needs to read as pressable against it (the pill's remove button).

overlay-active.$description: Pressed/selected wash — the highlighted option in a dropdown, a selected chip, a drag-over drop zone. DERIVED from the brand rather than fixed, so a spoke re-pointing --color-background-brand moves it too. It was rgba(0, 88, 98, 0.08), a teal left over from an older brand, which is why selected rows used to read cool in a green UI.

overlay-backdrop.$description: Scrim behind dialogs, side dialogs and the confirm dialog.

overlay-scrim.$description: Light counterpart to `overlay-backdrop` — veils content in place rather than behind a dialog, so what is underneath stays readable (the loading overlay).

min.$description: WCAG 2.5.5 floor. A role, not a ramp step — never re-point it smaller.

elevation.$description:
The shadow composites. Tier 1 holds the four axes as raw material (--shadow-offset-x / -offset-y-* / -blur-* / -spread-* / -color-*); clustering a particular combination and declaring it a resting card, a dropdown or a modal is the SEMANTIC act, so it happens here. This replaces the old --shadow-050…500 composites, which were ordinal names for intents sitting in tier 1 — the same misfiling as --transition-fast, and it left a 1:1 passthrough where every primitive had exactly one consumer. Those names still resolve via the deprecated aliases build.js emits from migrations.json (`shadow-composites-to-elevation`).

The axis steps keep their padded-ordinal names (050…500) because a tier-1 ramp is named that way, so elevation-4 reads the -300 step. The offset is not a mistake: the ramp has six steps and the roles have six jobs, and neither numbering should be bent to flatter the other.

HOVER IS NOT A RUNG. A hover lift moves an element ONE rung up from its resting rung — it is a transform on the ladder, not a place on it. Rung 3 used to be described as `Raised cards, hover state`, and being the only rung that named an interaction is exactly why it became the drawer everything lifted got thrown into: six dropdown surfaces sat on it instead of 4. Each rung now names a KIND OF SURFACE, and hover is derived.

1.$description: Resting lift — subtle depth for always-visible surfaces.

3.$description: Raised card — a surface sitting above the page but still part of it. Also the resting rung for a floating control that is not anchored to a trigger, like the back-to-top button. This used to read `Raised cards, hover state`, which was the one rung naming an interaction rather than a surface; see the HOVER rule on the group above.

4.$description: Anchored or transient floating surfaces — dropdowns, popovers, menus, tooltips, toasts. The whole family is named on purpose: when this said only `Dropdowns, popovers, menus`, six dropdown surfaces guessed and landed on 3, the tooltip landed on 2, and nothing agreed.

6.$description: Full-screen overlays that float above everything — the command palette, entity search. Deliberately heavier than the modal step.
